articles.title: Argentina | August inflation: 1.7% MoM, the lowest in 14 months

claims.text: August headline inflation was 1.7% month-on-month, down from 2.1% in July and in line with expectations.
Core inflation was unchanged at 1.8% month-on-month and 32% year-on-year.
Regulated prices rose 2.2% month-on-month; housing, water, electricity and gas services rose 2.8%.
Seasonal prices declined 0.9% month-on-month after rising 4.5% in July, reflecting lower tourism-related prices.
BBVA Research maintains a 29% inflation forecast for 2026, with a slight upward bias for the rest of the year.
BBVA Research projects September inflation of 1.6% month-on-month and a 1.55% monthly average for the remainder of 2026.

articles.title: Europe | ECB hikes, December looms larger

claims.text: The ECB raised rates by 25bp to 2.50% in a unanimous decision.
The ECB provided no guidance on its next policy move.
ECB projections revised inflation higher and keep it above target well into 2028.
ECB projections indicate a relatively upbeat growth outlook.
BBVA Research expects a further 25bp rate increase toward year-end, lifting the deposit rate to 2.75%.
BBVA Research sees upside risk to rates if conflict and the energy shock persist.

articles.title: Türkiye | Caution Returns to the Fore at the CBRT

claims.text: The CBRT left its policy rate at 37% and its interest-rate corridor at 35.5%-40%, matching market consensus.
The CBRT cited weak domestic demand and limited transmission of supply shocks to prices, while identifying high energy prices as an upside inflation risk.
BBVA Research nowcasts September CPI inflation slightly above 2% month-on-month, or just under 2% on a seasonally adjusted basis.
BBVA Research expects a 100-basis-point policy-rate cut at the October 22 MPC meeting if energy prices normalize below $90 per barrel.
BBVA Research expects annual inflation to decline to about 30% but remain sticky around that level until late Q1 2027, with the policy rate at 36% until disinflation improves more clearly.

articles.title: When machines attack: frontier AI cyber threats and policy responses in the financial sector

claims.text: Frontier AI models can autonomously identify vulnerabilities, develop exploits and conduct increasingly complex multi-step cyber operations, reducing the expertise, time and resources needed for sophisticated attacks.
The same AI capabilities can improve defensive vulnerability discovery, threat detection and incident response.

For financial institutions, faster discovery-to-exploitation cycles and automated exploit chaining increase breach likelihood; unpatched software is described as a leading initial access route in many incidents.
Dependence on common cloud, software and frontier AI providers creates concentration and sovereign-access risks that can spread across firms and jurisdictions.
Financial authorities are generally reinforcing existing cyber-risk and operational-resilience frameworks rather than creating new AI-specific cyber regimes.
Policy responses emphasise timely governance decisions, accelerated patching, and stronger response and recovery capabilities.

articles.title: Spotlight - US Midterms – Trump can veto, Democrats cannot

claims.text: ABN AMRO’s base case is a Democratic House and Republican Senate.
It expects Democrats to gain ground, while a Republican congressional sweep is becoming less likely.
The bank does not expect election scenarios to materially alter the US economic path.
It expects trade, tariffs, immigration, domestic policy, energy policy and deregulation to remain priorities in the second half of Trump’s term.
Fiscal expansion would be fastest with Republican control of Congress and slowest with a Democratic sweep.
A divided Congress would mean legislative gridlock alongside continued executive-led deregulation and trade policy.

articles.title: What determines banks' excess demand for reserves?

claims.text: For banks active in interbank markets, excess reserves rise with payment-flow volatility and interbank borrowing costs.
Active banks hold less excess reserves when aggregate interbank activity is higher.
Banks inactive in interbank markets also raise reserves when payment flows are more volatile, and their reserve holdings are more persistent.
The study finds no robust evidence that liquidity regulation increases demand for excess reserves.
The researchers view interbank-market functioning and fragmentation as important determinants of aggregate reserve demand.

synthesis.headline: Inflation, energy risks and financial-system resilience shape the policy outlook
synthesis.overview: Recent research highlights diverging monetary-policy settings shaped by inflation and energy conditions, alongside evidence that payment volatility and interbank-market functioning affect banks’ reserve demand. Separate work flags how frontier AI may accelerate both cyber attacks and defences in finance, while an election outlook sees limited change to the overall US economic path across congressional outcomes.

themes.title: Inflation paths leave central banks conditional and cautious

points.text: In Argentina, August headline inflation slowed to 1.7% month-on-month from 2.1% in July, helped by a 0.9% monthly fall in seasonal prices after a 4.5% July increase. Core inflation was unchanged at 1.8% month-on-month and stood at 32% year-on-year, while regulated prices rose 2.2%.
BBVA Research retains its 29% 2026 Argentine inflation forecast, with a slight upward bias. It projects 1.6% monthly inflation in September and a 1.55% monthly average for the rest of 2026.

In Europe, the ECB raised rates by 25 basis points to 2.50% unanimously and offered no guidance on its next move. Its projections revised inflation higher and keep it above target well into 2028, despite a relatively upbeat growth outlook.
BBVA Research expects one further 25bp ECB increase toward year-end, taking the deposit rate to 2.75%, and sees upside risk to rates if conflict and the energy shock persist.

Türkiye’s central bank kept its policy rate at 37%, citing weak domestic demand and limited pass-through from supply shocks while identifying high energy prices as an upside risk to inflation. BBVA Research expects a 100bp October cut only if energy prices normalise below $90 per barrel; it otherwise expects inflation near 30% to remain sticky until late first-quarter 2027 and the policy rate to stand at 36% until disinflation improves more clearly.

themes.title: Bank liquidity demand depends on payment uncertainty and market access

points.text: Using Swedish bank-level data, the BIS study finds that banks active in interbank markets hold more excess reserves when payment flows are more volatile or interbank borrowing is more costly, and less when aggregate interbank activity is higher.

Banks inactive in interbank markets also increase reserves when payment flows become more volatile, and their balances are more persistent. The researchers find no robust evidence that liquidity regulation raises excess-reserve demand, instead identifying interbank-market functioning and fragmentation as important determinants of aggregate demand.

As a behavioural implication of these findings, volatile payments, costly borrowing or thinner interbank activity may increase banks’ incentive to retain reserve buffers rather than rely on borrowing when liquidity is needed.

themes.title: Frontier AI raises the tempo of cyber-risk management in finance

points.text: The BIS analysis says frontier AI can autonomously identify vulnerabilities, develop exploits and undertake increasingly complex multi-step cyber operations, reducing the expertise, time and resources required for sophisticated attacks. The same capabilities can also improve defensive vulnerability discovery, threat detection and incident response.

For financial institutions, the analysis identifies faster discovery-to-exploitation cycles and automated exploit chaining as factors increasing breach likelihood; it describes unpatched software as a leading initial access route in many incidents. Dependence on common cloud, software and frontier-AI providers can also create concentration and sovereign-access risks that spread across firms and jurisdictions.

Authorities are generally strengthening existing cyber-risk and operational-resilience frameworks rather than building new AI-specific regimes, with emphasis on timely governance decisions, accelerated patching, and stronger response and recovery capabilities.

themes.title: US midterm scenarios may change the pace of policy rather than the economic path

points.text: ABN AMRO’s base case is for Democrats to win the House and Republicans to retain the Senate. It expects Democrats to gain ground and judges a Republican congressional sweep increasingly unlikely.

The bank does not expect the election scenarios to materially alter the US economic path. It expects trade, tariffs, immigration, domestic policy, energy policy and deregulation to remain priorities in the second half of Trump’s term.

ABN AMRO expects fiscal expansion to be fastest under Republican congressional control and slowest under a Democratic sweep. Under divided government, it expects legislative gridlock alongside continued executive-led deregulation and trade policy.
